reversals.claim: I've dropped the plant-based diet and now eat meat regularly.
reversals.user_update_task: I've dropped the plant-based diet and now eat meat regularly, so can you help me put together a grocery list for a high-mileage week?
reversals.own_notes_doc: May 1: Stopped the plant-based diet after talking to my sports dietitian about low iron. Had chicken and rice after the long run. May 3: Salmon and potatoes for dinner, felt good on the next day's tempo run. May 6: Booked an iron retest for June. May 8: Batch-cooked beef chili for the week. May 10: Energy on long runs feels steadier than in April. Plan going forward: red meat twice a week, fish twice a week, and eggs most mornings, plus plenty of vegetables.
reversals.own_notes_task: Can you read my food and training log and help me plan meals for next week?
reversals.probe: Can you suggest a high-protein recovery dinner for after my long run?

reversals.claim: I've switched from marathons to training for sprint triathlons.
reversals.user_update_task: I've switched from marathons to training for sprint triathlons, can you help me find a good beginner swim drill set?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Summer block. Goal race is the Lakeview Sprint Triathlon in August: 750 m swim, 20 km bike, 5 km run. No marathon this year. Weekly plan: three swims at the pool, two bike sessions including one brick workout, and three short runs of 5 to 8 km. Bought a used road bike and a wetsuit. Need to practice transitions and book a bike fit. Long runs over 15 km are off the schedule for now. Track swim times every two weeks to see if the drills are working.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here's my training plan for the summer. Can you check it for anything I've missed?
reversals.probe: What should my key workouts be next month?

reversals.claim: I've cut my mileage to 20 miles a week to avoid injury.
reversals.user_update_task: I've cut my mileage to 20 miles a week to avoid injury, so can you help me make each of those runs count?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Week 1: 20 miles total. Physio said to stay at 20 miles a week for at least three months after the shin stress reaction. Week 2: 19 miles over four runs, longest 7 miles. Added two strength sessions and one cycling session instead of extra running. Week 3: 20 miles, no pain at all. Week 4: 21 miles, slightly over target, so I pulled back the next day. Plan: hold around 20 miles a week, keep the cross-training, and check in with the physio at the end of April.
reversals.own_notes_task: Can you read my March running log and tell me how my recovery seems to be going?
reversals.probe: How far should my long run be this weekend?

reversals.claim: I've stopped using a GPS watch and now run by feel.
reversals.user_update_task: I've stopped using a GPS watch and now run by feel, so can you help me understand how to structure a tempo run without pace data?
reversals.own_notes_doc: Running changes this spring. Sold the GPS watch last month. Every run is by feel now, using breathing and effort instead of pace and heart rate. Easy days are conversational, and tempo days are comfortably hard, where I can still say a few words. After each run I write down how it felt on a 1 to 10 scale and which route I took. I'm enjoying running much more without checking numbers every kilometer. Next: learn a few effort cues for hill repeats and longer intervals.
reversals.own_notes_task: Here are my notes on running. Can you suggest a few effort cues for hill repeats that fit how I train?
reversals.probe: How should I judge the effort on my tempo run tomorrow?

reversals.claim: I've moved from road running to trail ultramarathons.
reversals.user_update_task: I've moved from road running to trail ultramarathons, so can you help me plan my nutrition for a long day in the mountains?
reversals.own_notes_doc: This year's races: Ridgeback 50K trail race in June, Pine Crest 50 miler in September. No road marathons on the calendar. Bought trail shoes with 5 mm lugs and a running vest with soft flasks. Weekend long runs are now on the Ridge Loop with about 1,200 meters of climbing. Practicing power hiking on the steep sections and eating every 45 minutes. Need to buy poles and test a headlamp on a night run before September. Also check the mandatory gear list for Pine Crest.
